solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Tropical bird repeated French word? (6)

indicatorNotes.repeated: says the one French word is written twice in a row

annotation.surface: A birdwatcher in the tropics hears a call that sounds like one French word said twice.
annotation.walkthrough: The motmot is a real Central and South American bird with a racket-shaped tail, and its name really does look like French doubled.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain naming: the motmot is a real bird of Central and South American forests, known for its racket-tipped tail.

entries.clue: Best alfresco celebration? (5)

annotation.surface: A voter picks the finest outdoor party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Best' reads as an adjective praising the party; it is the verb, to beat someone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to best a rival and to outdo one both mean to beat them.

entries.clue: Noblewoman advances south circling most of Scottish island (11)

indicatorNotes.circling: MARCHES goes round the island's letters

blocks.note: IONA, the island off Mull, without its last letter; it sits inside MARCH|ES
S = south, added at the end

annotation.surface: A noblewoman strides south on a march around a Hebridean island.
annotation.walkthrough: Iona is a small island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides, the standard crossword island alongside Arran and Skye.
annotation.definitionFit: A marchioness is a noblewoman, the wife of a marquess or a peeress in her own right.

entries.clue: Huge drawing spanning English river (8)

indicatorNotes.spanning: TOWING stretches across E and R, holding them inside

annotation.surface: A huge sketch shows a bridge across an English river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' suggests a picture, and 'spanning' a bridge; the drawing is the pulling kind, a tow.
annotation.definitionFit: Something towering is huge, rising high above others.

entries.clue: Funny rock-forming mineral buried in mountain pass (7)

indicatorNotes.buried in: MICA lies inside COL, as rock would be buried in a mountain

blocks.note: a col is a pass between peaks
mica, the flaky mineral found in granite

annotation.surface: A strange mineral turns up underground in an Alpine pass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Funny' reads as 'odd' describing the mineral; it is the definition, meaning amusing.
annotation.definitionFit: Comical means funny, causing laughter.

entries.clue: Shrewd childminder’s beginning to change (5)

indicatorNotes.to change: the first letter of NANNY is swapped for another

blocks.note: the N at the start of NANNY is changed to C
NANNY, a childminder, keeps the rest of its letters

annotation.surface: A sharp nanny is starting to alter her ways.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter comes in; the definition tells you, since only CANNY fits _ANNY and means shrewd.
annotation.definitionFit: Canny means shrewd, especially with money.

entries.clue: Plant gathered for those attending (7)

indicatorNotes.for those attending: those attending are listening, so the word is heard, not read

blocks.note: mustered = gathered, as troops are rallied; said aloud, it is also a condiment

annotation.surface: Flowers are collected for the guests at an event.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Those attending' looks like the guests the plant is for; attending also means paying heed, listening.
annotation.definitionFit: Mustard is a yellow-flowered plant whose seeds make the condiment.

entries.clue: Quackery Harry and Al can’t reform (11)

indicatorNotes.reform: the letters are formed again into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder; the apostrophe is ignored

annotation.surface: Two confirmed frauds, Harry and Al, are incapable of mending their ways.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: two quacks who can't reform are practising the very thing defined.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a quack is a charlatan, so quackery and charlatanry name the same fraudulent practice.

entries.clue: In a relaxed position retailing pork pies? (5)

blocks.note: pork pies = lies in Cockney rhyming slang; retailing = telling (again)

annotation.surface: A butcher lounges back while selling pork pies.
annotation.walkthrough: Pork pies is Cockney rhyming slang for lies, often shortened to porkies. Retail here means to recount a story, not to sell.
annotation.definitionFit: Lying means both reclining and telling untruths.

entries.clue: County arranged date and support for sleepers (8)

indicatorNotes.arranged: the letters of DATE are put in a new order

annotation.surface: A county council fixes the date for a rail project involving sleepers.
annotation.walkthrough: Bedfordshire is an English county, abbreviated Beds. Sleepers suggest railway timbers; here they are people asleep.
annotation.definitionFit: A bedstead is the frame of a bed, the support for those sleeping in it.

entries.clue: Weaver’s out of bed — get drinking! (7,2)

blocks.note: Nick Bottom, the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream

annotation.surface: Someone yells at a lazy weaver who has just got up to start drinking.
annotation.walkthrough: Bottom is the Shakespearean weaver who wears an ass's head; the capital W on 'Weaver' disguises the name.
annotation.definitionFit: "Bottoms up!" is a toast urging people to drink.

entries.clue: Stupid wee boy entertains dull individual (5)

indicatorNotes.entertains: the phrase holds the answer inside it, as a host holds guests

annotation.surface: A silly little boy puts on a show for a boring person.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer spans three words, starting on the last letter of 'Stupid'.
annotation.definitionFit: A dweeb is a dull, socially awkward person.

entries.clue: Terribly thin setter, last to teach fractions (11)

indicatorNotes.Terribly: the letters are jumbled, done terribly
indicatorNotes.last to: take only the final letter of 'teach'

annotation.surface: A gaunt puzzle-setter is the last person you'd pick to teach fractions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Last to teach' reads as 'the worst choice of teacher'; it means only the last letter of 'teach'.
annotation.definitionFit: Thirteenths are fractions, each one part in thirteen.

entries.clue: A new set in charge, pure and virtuous (7)

blocks.note: to set as a jelly does = to gel

annotation.surface: A fresh team takes over, claiming to be clean and honest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set' reads as a group of people; it is the verb, to firm up.
annotation.definitionFit: Angelic means pure and virtuous, like an angel.

entries.clue: Announce candidature? He’s not worth a flutter performing at Bayreuth? (5,4,3,2,3,4)

annotation.answer: THROW ONE'S HAT IN THE RING
annotation.definition2: He’s not worth a flutter performing at Bayreuth?

blocks.note: the idiom for entering a contest

blocks.clueFragment: He’s not worth a flutter performing at Bayreuth?
blocks.note: read literally: a no-hope 'throw-one' with a hat, singing in The Ring

annotation.surface: A would-be candidate is compared to a hopeless singer at the Wagner festival.
annotation.walkthrough: Bayreuth is the Bavarian town whose festival stages Wagner's Ring cycle, so a performer there is 'in The Ring'. A flutter is a small bet: the joke pictures a no-hoper appearing in the Ring.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from boxing, where a challenger once tossed a hat into the ring to accept a fight; now it means declaring oneself a candidate.

entries.clue: Warm and protective doctor introducing a major transport system (8)

indicatorNotes.introducing: to introduce is to bring in first, so MO leads the rest

blocks.note: THE, the word that singles out a chief example

annotation.surface: A kindly doctor is put in charge of launching a big new transit network.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Introducing' just puts MO first. RLY is the standard abbreviation for railway.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: warmth and protectiveness are the qualities people associate with a mother.

entries.clue: Reportedly a member runs over fast (7)

indicatorNotes.Reportedly: as it is said, so 'a leg' is taken by sound

blocks.note: a member = a leg, a limb

annotation.surface: News comes that a club member is dashing back quickly.
annotation.walkthrough: Runs and over are both cricket abbreviations. 'Fast' is the musical sense: allegro is a brisk tempo marking.
annotation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical direction meaning fast and lively.

entries.clue: British prime minister cut down in conflict (6)

indicatorNotes.cut down: ATTLEE is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: Clement ATTLEE, post-war Labour prime minister, without his final E

annotation.surface: A British premier is struck down during a war.
annotation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was the British Labour prime minister from 1945 to 1951.
annotation.definitionFit: A battle is a conflict between armed forces.

entries.clue: Eccentric old dean on front of cathedral furnished with pillars (10)

indicatorNotes.Eccentric: the letters are jumbled out of their usual order

annotation.surface: A peculiar elderly dean stands at the entrance of a pillared cathedral.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old' looks like part of the dean's description but belongs to the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Colonnaded means having a row of columns.

entries.clue: Secular priest’s love managed to embrace American conservative, we hear (9)

indicatorNotes.to embrace: RAN wraps round the letters that follow
indicatorNotes.we hear: TORY is taken by sound and spelt TORI

blocks.note: ran = managed, split R|AN to hold the rest

annotation.surface: A priest's sweetheart manages to hug a US right-winger, so people say.
annotation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of the British Conservative party. Oratorians are secular priests: they live in community but take no religious vows.
annotation.definitionFit: An Oratorian is a priest of the Oratory of St Philip Neri, a congregation of secular priests.

entries.clue: Copper stabs doctor in the manner of a horror novel (7)

indicatorNotes.stabs: CU is thrust into the letters, as a blade goes in

blocks.note: Cu, the chemical symbol for copper, goes into A|LA
à la = in the manner of

annotation.surface: A policeman knifes a medic, like a scene from a gothic thriller.
annotation.walkthrough: Copper reads as a policeman; it is the metal, Cu. Stabbing is fitting, as the vampire in the answer is himself killed by a stake.
annotation.definitionFit: Dracula is Bram Stoker's 1897 vampire horror novel.

entries.clue: Explicitness of photographic slide (12)

blocks.note: a positive image on clear film

annotation.surface: Someone praises how clearly a photo slide shows its subject.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses share the idea of seeing through: plain dealing, and film you hold up to the light.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of seeing through: openness that hides nothing, and a slide of clear film viewed against light.

entries.clue: New mate’s air primarily impressing plant (9)

indicatorNotes.New: the letters take a new arrangement

annotation.surface: A new partner's manner is striking a gardener as distinctive.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'mate's' is ignored, so the S joins the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Artemisia is a genus of aromatic plants including wormwood and tarragon.

entries.clue: Cultivated tips of younger allium plant (4,4)

indicatorNotes.Cultivated: the letters are worked over into a new shape
indicatorNotes.tips of: take the two end letters of 'younger'

annotation.surface: A gardener grows the shoots of a young onion-family plant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Allium' looks like the plant being defined, and 'tips' like its shoots; the allium is only fodder, and the definition is the bare word at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: The arum lily is a plant with a white trumpet-shaped spathe.

entries.clue: Reasonable-sounding rate for travelling (4)

indicatorNotes.sounding: the word for 'reasonable' is taken by its sound

annotation.surface: A ticket price seems reasonable enough.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reasonable-sounding' reads as 'seems fair'; the hyphen hides a homophone indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A fare is the price charged for a journey.

entries.clue: Type of hound going about in wickerwork cradle (8)

indicatorNotes.going about: to go about something is to go round it, so BASSET goes round IN

annotation.surface: A basset hound curls up in a wicker cot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link placing the hound in the cradle; it is the letters that go inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A bassinet is a hooded wicker cradle for a baby.

entries.clue: Impasse occurring when horse’s companion dislodges bishop (9)

indicatorNotes.dislodges: the B is knocked out of the word

blocks.note: a stablemate shares a horse's stable
B = bishop in chess notation, removed

annotation.surface: Deadlock ensues when a racehorse's companion unseats a clergyman.
annotation.walkthrough: Bishop is B in chess, apt because stalemate is itself a chess term.
annotation.definitionFit: A stalemate is an impasse, a position where no progress is possible.

entries.clue: Treatment for inflammation in young fowl with cold substance (8)

blocks.note: a poult is a young chicken or turkey

annotation.surface: A remedy for a sore chick involves something icy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' links the definition to the wordplay: the treatment is found in what follows.
annotation.definitionFit: A poultice is a soft moist mass applied to the body to relieve inflammation.

entries.clue: River vessel, one skirting the Italian bell towers (9)

indicatorNotes.skirting: I runs along the edge of IL, following it

blocks.note: a pan is a cooking vessel
I = one, set at the edge of IL

annotation.surface: A boat on a river passes an Italian town's bell towers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat on the river; it is a pan. Campanili is the Italian plural, so 'the Italian' hints at the answer too.
annotation.definitionFit: Campanili are bell towers, especially free-standing Italian ones.

entries.clue: Graduate in transport company having an important position (8)

annotation.surface: A graduate at a transport firm holds a senior post.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container indicator but simply supplies its own letters in order.
annotation.definitionFit: Mainline, as an adjective, means central or principal, having an important position.

entries.clue: Old Bill’s Cuban story circulating round US city? (12)

indicatorNotes.circulating: the letters move around into a new order
indicatorNotes.round: the story's letters go round LA before the mixing

annotation.surface: The police's account of a Cuban tale is making the rounds in an American city.
annotation.walkthrough: The Old Bill is British slang for the police.
annotation.definitionFit: A constabulary is a police force, which the Old Bill is.

entries.clue: Interfering with sound of gong a little (10)

indicatorNotes.sound of: the word for 'gong' is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a gong is a medal, in British slang

annotation.surface: Someone meddles by striking a gong softly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gong' suggests the percussion instrument, and 'sound of' its noise; a gong is British slang for a medal or honour.
annotation.definitionFit: Meddlesome means interfering in others' affairs.

entries.clue: Experienced organisation promoting peace leaves river (7)

indicatorNotes.leaves: UN goes away from the word

blocks.note: the UN, United Nations, is removed from the front

annotation.surface: A seasoned peace group departs from a river.
annotation.walkthrough: The Derwent is a river name found in several English counties, including Derbyshire and Cumbria.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Derwent is one of several English rivers of that name.

entries.clue: Mist one can break up on this side of the mountains (10)

annotation.definition: on this side of the mountains
annotation.surface: Fog clears on the near side of a mountain range.
annotation.walkthrough: The Latin cis- means 'on this side of', as in cisalpine.
annotation.definitionFit: A rare Latinate word: cis- means 'on this side' and montane 'of mountains', the counterpart of ultramontane.

entries.clue: Spongy sweet damages permit blocked by His Majesty (11)

indicatorNotes.blocked by: HM stands in the way inside ALLOW

blocks.note: allow = permit, with HM at its front

annotation.surface: A sweet shop's licence is refused by the King.
annotation.walkthrough: HM goes at the very start of ALLOW; 'blocked by' places it there. 'Damages' reads as a legal payout; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the marshmallow, once made from the marsh-mallow plant, is the classic soft spongy sweet.

entries.clue: Unexpectedly Laura sat in as one down under (12)

indicatorNotes.Unexpectedly: the letters come out in an unexpected order

annotation.surface: Laura surprisingly fills in for someone who has fallen ill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One down' reads like a crossword reference to 1 down, or someone depressed; down under means Australia and New Zealand.
annotation.definitionFit: An Australasian is someone from the region of Australia and New Zealand, down under.

entries.clue: Cloud identified by singer standing outside back of manor (11)

blocks.note: the last letter of manoR, inside ST|ATUS

annotation.surface: A singer spots a cloud from outside the rear of a country house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Standing outside' reads as one instruction; 'standing' is STATUS and 'outside' tells it to wrap round.
annotation.definitionFit: Altostratus is a grey sheet of mid-level cloud.

entries.clue: House doctor sits with a guitar (11)

indicatorNotes.doctor: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

annotation.surface: A GP relaxes at home strumming a guitar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'House' is the astrological sense: one of the twelve houses, or signs, of the zodiac. 'Doctor' is a verb here, not a medic.
annotation.definitionFit: Sagittarius is one of the twelve signs, or houses, of the zodiac.

entries.clue: Innards of wading bird initially scanned by hospital department (8)

annotation.surface: A hospital unit X-rays the insides of a heron.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By' says the hospital department comes alongside, here in front.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: innards and entrails both mean an animal's guts.

entries.clue: Oil producer left half of France under the protection of two lots of crack troops (9)

indicatorNotes.left half of: keep the left half of FRANCE
indicatorNotes.under the protection of: the second SAS wraps round FRA, sheltering it

blocks.note: the SAS, the British special forces
a second SAS, split SA|S round FRA
the first three of the six letters of FRANCE

annotation.surface: An oil company flees half of France guarded by two units of elite soldiers.
annotation.walkthrough: The SAS (Special Air Service) is the British army's special forces regiment. 'Left' reads as 'departed'; it picks out the left-hand half of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: The sassafras tree yields an aromatic oil from its root bark.

entries.clue: One who is sustained by hill dwellers? (8)

annotation.definition: One who is sustained by hill dwellers?

blocks.clueFragment: One who is sustained by hill dwellers?
blocks.note: the surface suggests someone supported by mountain folk, as a patron or a charity case
the dwellers are ants in anthills, and 'sustained by' means fed on

annotation.surface: A person lives off the support of a hill community.
annotation.walkthrough: The hills are anthills. The question mark flags that the definition is playful.
annotation.definitionFit: An anteater feeds on ants, the dwellers in anthills.

entries.clue: Smooth-talking, reflecting a lot of rubbish (4)

indicatorNotes.reflecting: the letters are mirrored, read backwards
indicatorNotes.a lot of: most of BILGE, dropping its last letter

annotation.surface: A slick talker is showing a lot of nonsense.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: glib talk is often a lot of rubbish.
annotation.definitionFit: Glib means smooth-talking, fluent but insincere.

entries.clue: Piece of mail inviting depravity, do we hear? (8)

indicatorNotes.do we hear?: asks whether the words sound like the answer

annotation.surface: A letter arrives that seems to solicit wickedness.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piece of mail' reads as one item of post; 'Piece' alone is the definition, a piece of music.
annotation.definitionFit: A postlude is a concluding piece of music, often played at the end of a church service.

entries.clue: Hard-hearted behaviour not encountered by Naomi? (12)

blocks.note: Naomi's daughter-in-law Ruth stayed with her, so Naomi never went without Ruth

annotation.surface: A cruel attitude is something Naomi never met.
annotation.walkthrough: In the Book of Ruth, Naomi's daughter-in-law Ruth refuses to leave her, so Naomi never knew Ruthlessness.
annotation.definitionFit: The first half is a plain synonym for cruelty; the second jokes that Ruth never left Naomi, so Naomi was never without her.

entries.clue: Posh old man penning unfinished song in Swedish city (7)

indicatorNotes.penning: PA holds the song inside, as a pen holds animals

blocks.note: pa = father, split P|A round the song

annotation.surface: A well-to-do father writes an incomplete song while in a Swedish city.
annotation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is a crossword convention from the 1950s 'U and non-U' debate. Uppsala is Sweden's old university city.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this city north of Stockholm is Sweden's fourth largest and its oldest university seat.

entries.clue: Rabbit on in bed, ultimately about story read out loud (10)

indicatorNotes.read out loud: TALE is taken by its sound and spelt TAIL

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed

annotation.surface: A child in bed keeps chattering while a bedtime story is read.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit on' looks like the British phrase for talking at length; only 'Rabbit' is the definition, and 'on' supplies ON. 'In' just places the pieces together.
annotation.definitionFit: A cottontail is an American rabbit with a white fluffy tail.

entries.clue: Officer picked up slender Irish girl (7)

indicatorNotes.picked up: heard, as a radio picks up a signal

annotation.surface: A military officer collected a slim young woman from Ireland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' reads as collecting someone, or a romantic pick-up; it signals sound.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: the word comes from the Irish cailín, girl, and in English names an Irish girl.

entries.clue: Pair inside saw first of lags fall headlong (6)

indicatorNotes.inside: inside means within, so PR sits within SAW

blocks.note: a saw, split S|AW round PR

annotation.surface: Two convicts spot the leading old lag take a tumble.
annotation.walkthrough: An old lag is British slang for a long-term prisoner. 'Saw' reads as the past tense of see; it is the tool.
annotation.definitionFit: To sprawl can mean to fall so as to lie spread out, headlong.

entries.clue: Organ recorded in concert room’s entrance (5)

indicatorNotes.entrance: take the letter at the entrance, the start, of 'room'

blocks.note: a live recording is made in concert

annotation.surface: An organ performance is taped at the entrance to a concert hall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Organ' and 'concert room' conjure a musical instrument; the organ is a body part.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the liver is one of the body's vital organs, not the musical kind the surface suggests.

entries.clue: Clothing produced by learner after a quiet shave (7)

annotation.surface: A trainee turns out clothes after a quick, silent shave.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the learner's L at the end. 'Shave' is paring, not a razor.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, slightly formal: apparel is clothing, especially as sold in shops or worn for show.

entries.clue: Endlessly lie around idly in Pennsylvania square (5)

indicatorNotes.in: in means within, so LAZ sits within PA

blocks.note: PA, the state abbreviation, split P|A
to laze = to lie around idly, without its final E

annotation.surface: Loafers lounge forever in a Pennsylvania town square.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lie around idly' is one definition of LAZE, not a separate instruction to reverse.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowing: plaza is Spanish for a town square, used in English for an open public space.

entries.clue: New pamphlet going into extremely effective interval music (8)

indicatorNotes.going into: going into means entering, so N and TRACT enter between the two Es

blocks.note: the outer letters of EffectivE, split E|E

annotation.surface: A fresh leaflet proves very effective during a concert interval.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' reads as 'very'; it means the two ends of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: An entr'acte is music played between the acts of a play or opera.

entries.clue: Woman’s article accepted by European journal finally (5)

indicatorNotes.accepted by: THE is taken in between E and L

annotation.surface: A woman's piece is taken by a European magazine at last.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' reads as a written piece for the journal; it is the grammatical article THE.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Ethel is a woman's first name, standing in for any woman, a common crossword device.

entries.clue: Cross about holding up children’s game (5)

indicatorNotes.holding up: in a down answer, TIG sits on top of ON

annotation.surface: Someone gets angry about delays to a playground game.
annotation.walkthrough: Tig is the British name for the playground chasing game tag. 'Cross' reads as angry; it is a hybrid animal.
annotation.definitionFit: A tigon is a cross between a male tiger and a lioness.

entries.clue: Throughout pub, mainly after that clamour is almost done (3,4,3,3,8)

indicatorNotes.mainly: THEN keeps most of its letters, losing the last

blocks.note: after that = THEN, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Across the pub, the noise mostly dies down once last orders are called.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pub, mainly' looks like it trims BAR; 'mainly' belongs to 'after that'. The answer's 'is' makes the definition a verb phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: "It's all over bar the shouting" means the result is settled and the thing is almost done.

entries.clue: Increase has desired outcome for Madame Tussauds for example (8)

blocks.note: to wax = to grow, as the moon does
it works = it has the desired effect

annotation.surface: A growth in visitors pays off for a famous London tourist attraction.
annotation.walkthrough: Madame Tussauds is the London museum of wax figures of celebrities.
annotation.definitionFit: A waxworks is a museum of wax figures, such as Madame Tussauds.

entries.clue: Way to make a comeback with introduction of a Royal Society magazine (7)

indicatorNotes.introduction of: A and RS are put at the front

blocks.note: a lane is a way, reversed

annotation.surface: A scientific society's magazine plans a revival.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' reads as a periodical; it is a store for weapons and ammunition. A football fan also sees Arsenal making a comeback.
annotation.definitionFit: A second sense of magazine: a store for weapons and ammunition, not a periodical.

entries.clue: Jewish ascetic originally enchanted by German city (6)

blocks.note: the first letter of Enchanted, placed by the city

annotation.surface: A devout hermit is charmed by a German city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By' means next to, so the E sits beside ESSEN, here after it.
annotation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect around the time of Christ.
